english_translation.text: Individual souls possess immortality through theosis.

philosophical_theme: CLUSTER: Celestial hierarchy — Daemons, angels, intelligences, their roles and natures; cosmic ordering
plotinian_parallel: Enneads 3.5 (Daemons), 5.5 (Intelligible world and cosmos), Porphyry *On Abstinence* III (daemon theory)
charge: The doctrine of soul's descent into body and materiality potentially implies necessity rather than divine will.
defense: Soul's descent is voluntary and recuperative (soul purifies matter through organizing and enlivening it). Follows Plotinian and Porphyrian psychology.
heretical_notes: Daemon and angel theses likely connected to heretical Q5 (magic/theurgy). Copenhaver analyzes these in context of theurgic innovation and magic trial. Check whether Iamblichan theurgy (ritual invocation of daemons) appears here; if so, mark for heretical essay.
notes: T61–T80 address celestial beings and intermediary powers. CRITICAL for heretical essay: theurgy, daemon magic, and theurgic innovation are condemned (Q5). Pico draws on Iamblichus *De Mysteriis* and Proclus's henad theory. Daemon theses intersect with Kabbalah (sefirot as intermediaries). Check for 'divine names' language (sign of theurgic engagement).

exegesis: Pico's conclusion on Intellect within the Neoplatonism tradition.
